# Independent audit: original-volume row entropy and rank-one label geometry

Targets:

- `candidate 9e43ca1dd488e8cb`, Sections 1--4.
- `candidate 50a9575831060dc5`, Sections 1--5.

Result: full independent PASS. No repair identified. Neither source
promotes the conditional transport to a class Gamma payment.

## 1. Original-volume row identities

The ratio d(bar rho_i)/d rho_i=L/L_i is normalized by the actual L
martingale moment. Multiplication by sigma_i and summation recovers
exactly dm/M, so no source or target mass is lost. On row i, contact with
an active affine plane gives L-L_i=a_i dot(w-Y_i). Multiplication by the
centered vector and integration yields Cov(rho_i) a_i/L_i, including
the base/continuous cross covariance. A different active plane has zero
centered difference almost surely on that same row and therefore gives
the same covariance vector.

The directional mean defect equals Var(L)/L_i, which proves all equality
equivalences (6), even if the covariance matrix is singular. The KL
identity uses the original mixed log normalization, not tilted log
normalization. Its exact weighted sum is -sum sigma_i log L_i. Taylor
comparison for s log s on [l_i/L_i,U_i/L_i] gives precisely the factors
1/(2L_i U_i) and 1/(2L_i l_i) in (10). The final mean decomposition (11)
retains all covariance corrections and cannot be simplified by a common
sign of their vectors.

A positive row with nonzero continuous active-plane gradient cannot be
confined to a constant L level: that plane level is null in every sampled
fiber. This proves the strict entropy assertion using actual target
absolute continuity. Its converse is correctly not claimed.

## 2. Closed source classes and parity

For an integer anchored combination of proper sources, convex buffered
superlevels and the strict pure-base gap place the averaged mark in the
proper deepest stratum. Exact quantile equality forces f equality and
then L equality. Every target active PL plane touches each positive
input and inherits its unique continuous gradient. Thus the enlarged
source-gradient set is a closed minor. The midpoint version proves
parity disjointness without needing positive sigma at the midpoint.

## 3. One-source label and the continuous target

If a label has exactly one positive source, the sum of all allocation
functions is one and each preserves its label. Consequently that source
allocation is one almost everywhere on its label and zero off it.
Contact with any source plane identifies its target measure with the
restriction of original mixed measure to the convex set D_i={A_i=L}.
Conversely all positive-volume fiber-interior points of this set, except
the finite continuous-gradient tie hyperplanes, have that label.

This is sufficient for exact equality of d-dimensional measures in
every sampled fiber. It does not require pointwise equality at the fiber
boundary. The actual sections of D_i are compatible by convexity. Their
sampled canonical hull has exactly the same integer sections: the hull
is contained in D_i and contains each original sampled section. Its
integer projection remains lattice-complete. Positivity is inherited
under anchored combinations by combining balls in the input sections,
so the positive-volume bases form a closed minor as stated.

## 4. Rank-one conclusion and higher-rank limitation

In a complete rank-one lattice, an interval between two distinct source
bases contains both inherited parities. Closure of one gradient-source
class therefore excludes any other label. When there are at least two
labels, each has exactly one positive source, and the preceding convex
representative theorem applies. A sole label has the original C as its
representative even if it has several positive sources. This proves the
rank-at-most-one statement without an unnecessary one-source assumption.

For higher rank, the fiber maximum F_c(z)=max_X[L-c dot X] is concave,
but the anchored maximizer inclusion needs equality of F_c along that
specific relation. The displayed equality condition (8) is sufficient
by the two matching bounds. Rowwise contact supplies this condition only
inside that row's base contact face. The source correctly refuses to
combine different rows through an unproved equality.

Compatibility of label representatives alone still does not justify a
source-parity class payment, as the independently audited ten-base
interval example demonstrates.
